newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ends bourse at record, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: German ends bourse at record, seen consolidating.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares ended floor trade on Friday at a new record level, supported by strength on other bourses, the firm dollar and data showing improved domestic business confidence.

But the IBIS DAX, which measures all-day computerised trading in the DAX, ended slightly off record highs as Wall Street lost some ground in early dealings. IBIS closed at 2,727.56, up 10.06, or 0.37 percent.
The DAX index earlier closed bourse trade up 18.56 points, or 0.68 percent, at 2,734.20, slightly off the day's high of 2,739.26.
Dealers said they expected the market to consolidate around these new levels next week, before moving ahead.

"The market in general could try slowly but surely inch up higher. Most people now are turning positive on Germany, even some of the old bears," said one dealer. "But we might need some sideways consolidation first."
Among individual shares, car maker Daimler Benz continued to be a favourite and closed IBIS trade up 0.80 marks at 89.75 marks.
Mercedes-Benz, part of the Daimler group, said sales for commercial vehicles had risen five percent to 248,600 vehicles for the first nine months of 1996.

Sportsware firm Adidas was one of Friday's main movers, dropping sharply in early trade, but ending IBIS trade down just three marks at 139 marks. "There are rumours that earnings downgrades are in the pipeline," said one trader.

New stock dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care, which was spilt off from medical products group Fresenius AG early this month, added over nine percent, to end electronic trade 11.25 marks higher at 136.
"This is a second chance to enter the Fresenius empire," said one dealer. "Fresenius AG has also made gains this year."
Dealers said the publication of the price range for shares in soon to be floated national telecommunications monopoly Deutsche Telekom would be a focus on Monday.
